Remark
[role of segments in the proof]

Source: petersen:page-0470 ↗ thm:pet-ch12-toponogov 1. ch12:12.2.5The proof never uses that the objects being compared in $M$ are segments; it only requires that the geodesics used in $S_k^n$ are segments. For $k\le 0$ this is automatic. For $k>0$ it means the comparison geodesic must have length $<\pi /\sqrt k$, the condition used in the $k=1$ case of the proof.
